identity.name: Reformed Government of the Republic of China
native_names: 中華民國維新政府 (Zhōnghuá Mínguó Wéixīn Zhèngfǔ)
identity.wikipedia: Reformed Government of the Republic of China

land.text: the page: 'assigned control of the provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui as well as the two municipalities of Nanjing and Shanghai'

predecessors.note: The Republic of China dossier (ea-08-c) records this land as Japanese occupation from December 1937, not as this state's land.

land.text: 'merged into Wang Jingwei's Nanjing-based Reorganized National Government on 30 March 1940'

capitals.name: Nanjing
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Nanjing; the government was founded 'at the National Great Hall'.

correction.text: Jiangsu, Anhui, Shanghai and the north of Zhejiang, with Nanjing as capital

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row for this regime. The Reformed Government page says it 'was assigned control of the provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui as well as the two municipalities of Nanjing and Shanghai'; the Reorganized National Government page says its successor 'controlled only Jiangsu, Anhui, and the north sector of Zhejiang' at formation. The shape follows the second (what was held): Jiangsu, Anhui, Shanghai and a northern strip of Zhejiang (118.3-122.6 E, 29.9-31.5 N, the researcher's reading of 'north sector'). The infobox gives no area or population.

region.text: Jiangsu, Anhui, Shanghai and the north of Zhejiang

ledger.note: 28 March 1938: 'established by Liang Hongzhi and others on 28 March 1938 at the National Great Hall' (Nanjing per the infobox capital), 'assigned control of the provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui as well as the two municipalities of Nanjing and Shanghai'. The Reorganized National Government page (successor) says it held Jiangsu, Anhui and the north sector of Zhejiang; the shape follows that. Confidence 2: 'assigned' is not 'held'.

region.text: all of the Reformed Government's land

ledger.note: 30 March 1940: 'merged into Wang Jingwei's Nanjing-based Reorganized National Government on 30 March 1940'; the Reorganized National Government page: 'The RNG absorbed the Reformed Government (1938-1940) and the Provisional Government (1937-1940)'.

wars.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
wars.outcome: The regime was run under Japanese army oversight (the page names the Japanese Central China Area Army, which drafted plans in December 1937, and advisers from the China Expeditionary Army) with about 10,000 men at creation and about 30,000 by 1939; it merged into Wang Jingwei's government on 30 March 1940.
wars.note: The war itself was not opened for this dossier.

certainty.note: The page assigns three provinces and two cities; the successor page says only Jiangsu, Anhui and the north of Zhejiang were held; no towns or lines are named.

sources.title: Reformed Government of the Republic of China
sources.note: Founding 28 March 1938; assigned provinces and municipalities; merger 30 March 1940; Liang Hongzhi; silent on area and population.

sources.title: Reorganized National Government of China
sources.note: The successor's initial control (Jiangsu, Anhui, north Zhejiang) and the absorption of the Reformed Government.

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from two pages (a 2-year state, below the ten-year bar, written because the Reorganized National Government's dossier names it as its predecessor). Not settled: (1) 'assigned control' of Zhejiang versus the successor page's 'north sector of Zhejiang': the shape follows the successor page, with a strip the researcher drew; (2) the page gives no area or population; (3) the page is silent on Beijing; the Provisional Government (Dec 1937) is only named as the separate northern administration. (4) The Republic of China (ea-08-c) and Empire of Japan (jk-01-d) dossiers carry Shanghai, Nanjing and the lower Yangtze as Japanese occupation from 1937-12 and have no event naming this state; a reviewer should decide whether to add a loss for the Republic and a vassal_start for Japan. Gazetteer: the strip of northern Zhejiang is a polygon.
